_comment: Canonical-facts registry for Praxis. Machine-checkable single-source-of-truth guards consumed by validate-plugin.sh (Phase 1). Extend forbiddenTerms as terminology evolves.

forbiddenTerms.reason: wave product-architecture is 'the educated theory', not 'the bet'
mantra is 'Wave = educated theory; capability record = truth'
renamed to 'four-condition disjointness' (the rule has four conditions)
canonical test pyramid is Logic -> Composition -> Adapter Contract -> Integration -> Journey

the lite/standard adoption profile dial was cut pre-release (never shipped in a tagged version, confirmed via git merge-base against v0.3.0) -- full is the only supported profile; do not reintroduce without real-repo evidence per the evolution policy
the three-way adoption-profile enum was cut pre-release; full is the only supported profile
meta-commentary anti-pattern: defensive throat-clearing that pre-empts an unmade challenge. State the reason as a bare flat assertion instead.

_placeholderKeys: TS.260823.08: the authority for what a template may substitute is the engine's adoption Binding, not one of the templates. It used to be the config template, on the premise that it declared every key — true while every key was a config key, and false the moment the verify and overlay templates started carrying stack facts the config never holds. Declared once here; the shell lint checks the templates against it and a Rust test checks the Binding against it, so a key added to one and not the other fails on both sides.

requiredPhrases.reason: README's opening pitch must disclose that not every gate is equally binding, so an adopter does not over-trust a green check. The pattern is the honesty CLAIM rather than the list — the list was three kinds, is four since the delivery graph, and encoding a count in a check makes the check stale the next time the truth improves.

requiredPhrases.pattern: would import those claims without their evidence
requiredPhrases.reason: TS.260823.08: adoption writes a binding and a checkable empty record, and never a transcription of what the repository already claims. That is the longest argument this skill makes and the front door contradicted it for two versions — both entry points scaffolded a whole product tree. The phrase is what the check can hold; the failure mode is not a missing warning but a confident scaffold.
